The AMS Feeder Unit is specially designed to support the AMS for printing multiple colors and materials. Each AMS has 4 feeder units, and each feeder unit has its own motor and gears to actively push the filament forward or wind it back to the spool. The AMS Feeder Unit has a sensor to detect filament. When a filament is inserted, the feeder unit will pull the filament automatically. When a filament needs to be winded back, the feeder unit will drive the AMS driving sleeve to rotate the spool for filament winding.
Learn more about the replacement of AMS Feeder Unit (Hall) on Bambu Lab Wiki.
Plastic, PCBA

The Bambu Lab AMS Feeding Funnel is one of the components of the AMS First Stage Feeder, which consists of structural parts and a filament detection sensor board. When the sensor board detects the insertion of filament, the AMS first stage feeder will pull the filament forward automatically. When the filament insertion is abnormal, the sensor board will also identify it and feed that information back to the 3D printer.
Learn more about the replacement of AMS feeding funnel on Bambu Lab Wiki.

The ceramic heater and thermistor for Bambu Lab P1P are combined into one module with an integrated terminal connector. With this design, the reliability of the terminal connector under extreme conditions is improved. The ceramic heater can heat the nozzle up to 300℃ while the Hotend Thermistor has highly accurate temperature measurement and reliable structural design. The Ceramic Heater & Thermistor is for use with Bambu nozzle assemblies only.

strings.en: The cooling fan is used for cooling and reducing the temperature of the ceramic heater for hotend. In addition, the cooling fan for our hotend has an auto-shutoff after being locked at rated voltage for 1-3 seconds. The circuit attempts to restart in 2 to 6 seconds. There is no damage after 72 hours of locking. Warning: The cooling fan is a high-speed rotating part, so do not touch it while it is running.

The Bambu Hardened Steel Extruder Gear Assembly is one of the components of the Bambu Hardened Steel Extruder Unit. Consisting of the driven gear and the active gear, the extruder gear assembly can feed filament into the hotend. Although it is constructed with heavy-duty parts for a long service life, the extruder gear assembly can be replaced if abrasion happens after long-term use. It's not only suitable for feeding common 3D printing filaments, but also for feeding engineering filaments like carbon fiber nylon, glass fiber nylon, etc.
Learn more about the replacement of hardened steel extruder gear on Bambu Lab Wiki.

The AMS Lite Rotary Spool Holder is designed to support and hold the spool when it's attached to the AMS Lite. Each rotary spool holder has 3 spool claws to secure the spool in place. While the feeder unit pulls the filament, the rotary spool holder works in coordination to enable the spool to rotate during the printing process. This ensures continuous filament feeding and smooth operation. The rotary spool holder is designed in both green and yellow versions to work with the left and right feeder units for filament feeding. For the green version, the two holders are installed on the bottom-right roller and top-left roller, rotating counterclockwise to feed filament to slots 1 and 3. For the yellow version, the two holders are installed on the bottom-left roller and top-right roller, rotating clockwise to feed filament to slots 2 and 4. Learn more about replacing the AMS lite Rotary Spool Holder on Bambu Lab Wiki.

The AMS Lite Spool Claw is assembled on the Rotary Spool Holder and is used to secure the spool in place. The 3 rubber pads on the claws are used to increase the friction between the claws and the spool, preventing the spool from detaching from the spool holder during the printing process. It is imperative to replace the X Belt promptly in cases of severe wear or breakage to avoid operational disruptions of the printer. C

The AMS Lite 4-pin cable is used to connect the A1 mini main unit and the AMS Lite device. It serves two functions: providing power from the A1 mini to the AMS Lite and facilitating communication between the two devices. This enables the A1 mini to control the AMS Lite, allowing it to read information from the filament spool RFID tag and manage the switching/extrusion of multi-color 3D printing consumables.
